answer: A fable warns that cheap masks invite fraud, so an agent economy can demand each identity stake a small deposit bound to a unique cipher key that signs every transaction. Reputation then accrues only to that key, like a comet leaving one trail, so an attacker who splits into many fake agents must lock up a deposit and build history for each one. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents pay once and keep earning trust.
